name: UK benefit uprating — September 2026 CPI (ONS outturn and OBR's March 2026 forecast), and PolicyEngine-UK's benefit rates against the published April upratings
organization: Office for National Statistics (CPI); Office for Budget Responsibility (forecast)
access_note: obr.uk returns a Cloudflare challenge to scripted fetches; the OBR workbook is the Wayback Machine capture of 2026-04-23 (web.archive.org/web/20260423152500id_/https://obr.uk/docs/d055fbf02d5b3g6jq8l2/efo-march-2026-detailed-forecast-tables-economy.xlsx). The ONS JSON is the series' own data endpoint.

model.name: ONS Consumer Prices Index (outturn); OBR March 2026 economy forecast
model.method: D7G7 is the CPI all-items 12-month rate as published (ONS does not revise published CPI). OBR Table 1.7 forecasts the CPI year-on-year growth by quarter; 2026 Q3 holds the September the April 2027 uprating uses.
model.method_basis: ONS D7G7 metadata; EFO March 2026 detailed forecast tables, economy, Table 1.7

boundary_note: The ONS rate is an official outturn, which the 2026-08-02 boundary rule sends to the Chronicle ledger. It is staged as a claim by decision (2026-10-22), as the Census STC collections were on #176: September CPI is the threshold an April uprating is judged against, and PolicyEngine-UK has a direct counterpart, its own April 2027 uprating.
attaches_to: The lane also attaches PolicyEngine-UK read-backs to the HM Treasury Budget 2025 uprating claims (lane uk-ab2025-official) and the Resolution Foundation uprating claims (lane uk-thinktanks); it never edits those claims.
diagnosis_upstream: A gap between PolicyEngine-UK's uprating inputs and the published rates is an input-currency issue in policyengine-uk (gov.economic_assumptions), reported upstream.
